samples.summary: Revision-preview snapshot reader recurses over the whole peer-written docs tree with no depth cap, bypassing the MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH guard this PR wires up
samples.evidence:
The guard this PR establishes (`packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26`, applied at `crdt-tree.ts:225` and `yorkie-doc-store.ts:480`) exists, by its own file header, because "a peer can write that chain to any depth it likes with plain Tree writes" and overflow the stack of every reader. One reader is not covered: `parseDocsSnapshot` (snapshot-adapters.ts:169) runs `normalizeYsonTreeNode(root.content.root)` FIRST (line 178), and that function recurses unconditionally on `node.children.map(normalizeYsonTreeNode)` at line 140 with no depth parameter and no ceiling. `docsTreeToDocument`'s cap only runs on the already-fully-normalized tree, so it can never prevent the overflow.

Vector: a collaborator (or anyone who can drive the REST/Yorkie write path outside the v1 `assertValidBlock` depth check — e.g. a direct Yorkie Tree write from a browser session, which is not validated by the backend at all) writes `block > row > cell > block > table > …` a few tens of thousands deep. A revision snapshot capturing that document is then served to any viewer who opens revision history; `normalizeYsonTreeNode` blows the stack with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the cap is reached. `RevisionPreview` may surface it as an alert, but the reader is exactly the "one peer's write hangs everyone's tab" hazard the constant is documented to close, now left open on the one reader that parses a snapshot instead of a live proxy. Note `unwrapYsonScalars`' `walk` deliberately returns `Tree` subtrees by reference (unwrap-yson.ts:98), so nothing else bounds this walk either.

Fix direction: thread a depth counter through `normalizeYsonTreeNode` and stop (or throw a handled error) at the same ceiling `docsTreeToDocument` uses, so the two halves of the preview reader are bounded identically.

samples.summary: unwrapYsonScalars' walk() recurses uncapped over peer-controlled snapshot JSON, running before the depth-capped slides band and defeating it
samples.evidence:
`walk()` recurses on every array element (line 95) and every object value (line 106) of a `YSON.parse`d revision snapshot with no depth bound. The slides model explicitly acknowledges the threat — `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:36` says "the `data.children` chain a peer wrote can be arbitrarily deep" and `bandElementNumerics` therefore stops at `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` (line 112). But `parseSlidesSnapshot` (snapshot-adapters.ts:52-56) and `parseBoardSnapshot` (line 72) call `unwrapYsonScalars(YSON.parse(snapshot))` BEFORE `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`, so the uncapped `walk` traverses the same arbitrarily deep `data.children` chain first and overflows the stack before the capped band ever runs.

Vector: a peer writes a deeply nested group chain (or any deeply nested object) into a deck/board root via direct Yorkie writes; any user who opens revision history for that document crashes the preview with a stack overflow. I confirmed the recursion is uncapped and that group nesting is a real, peer-writable shape (`GroupElement.data.children: Element[]`, packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:402); I did not measure the exact depth at which V8 overflows, hence medium confidence on exploitability rather than on the missing bound.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as claimed — `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143) recurses unconditionally at line 140 with no depth cap, and `parseDocsSnapshot` (line 178) runs it before `docsTreeToDocument`, so the MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH cap in crdt-tree.ts:219-229 cannot prevent the deep walk. However, the security impact asserted is not reachable. I enumerated every call site of `parseDocsSnapshot`: the only production caller is `parseByType` at revision-preview.tsx:88, invoked at revision-preview.tsx:213 inside an explicit try/catch (lines 212-221) whose handler sets `error` and renders the `role="alert"` "Couldn't read this version" branch (lines 313-320). A stack overflow in JS throws a catchable RangeError; the stack unwinds completely back to line 214 (the recursion is pure and synchronous, holding no locks or partial state), so the caught path runs with a full stack. The remaining call sites are tests only (__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts:223,344,353,366). The realized worst case is therefore: a collaborator who already has write access to a document makes that same document's revision preview display an error message instead of content, to users who already have access to it. That is a recoverable, self-scoped availability degradation — no authorization bypass, no secret/sensitive-data exposure, no injection, no broken signature/HMAC or constant-time issue, no SSRF or path traversal. The "one peer's write hangs everyone's tab" hazard the constant documents is closed at this caller by the catch. Under the Security rubric this does not rise to critical (no exploitable vuln) or major (no clear security weakness); it is at most a hardening nit, and the "bound both halves of the reader identically" argument belongs to the correctness/robustness lens.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described — `walk()` at unwrap-yson.ts:92-108 recurses uncapped (array at line 95, object values at line 105), and parseSlidesSnapshot/parseBoardSnapshot (snapshot-adapters.ts:52-56, 71-72) do run it before the depth-capped `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` (band-numerics.ts:40,112). A V8 stack-overflow RangeError is an ordinary catchable throw and the stack has unwound before that synchronous catch runs, so the outcome is the documented unreadable-snapshot path: a `role="alert"` "Couldn't read this version" panel (revision-preview.tsx:313-320) over a still-mounted live editor, with Back/Restore/navigation still rendered from `meta` (lines 244-296). The realistic worst case is therefore: a peer who already holds write access to the shared document makes one revision preview show an error instead of content — identical to the malformed-snapshot behaviour the module explicitly designs for (snapshot-adapters.ts:36-39). searchedFor: Grep computeSelectionRects call sites in editor.ts
finding.summary: Clamping bounds the rectangle to the table, but the table size is itself peer-chosen and `expandCellRangeForMerges` is an O(area) fixed-point scan run once per paint per peer selection
finding.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` clamps `start`/`end` to the table and then calls `expandCellRangeForMerges(ordered, table)` (line 146), a `while (changed)` loop whose inner `for (r) for (c)` scans the whole rectangle each pass. `normalizeRange` is reached from `computeSelectionRects`, which `editor.ts:2098` calls once per peer per paint (and `getSelectionRects` calls for the local selection). Row count is not banded anywhere — `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` (numeric-attrs.ts:95) caps columns at 256 but nothing caps `rows.length` — so a peer who writes a very large table and publishes `tableCellRange` `{start:{0,0}, end:{1e9,1e9}}` gets clamped to the *full table* and then re-scanned each frame, including on paint-only renders where the table layout is not recomputed. `maxCol` additionally reduces over every row on each call. Residual, not introduced: the change also newly routes *nested* tables into this expansion via the `resolveNestedTableLayout` fallback (line 191), widening what reaches it. A cheap fix is to cap the clamped rectangle's area (or the fixed-point pass count) rather than only its indices.

verdict.reason: Verified in the tree. selection.ts:132-147 clamps the peer-supplied rectangle only to the table's own dimensions and then calls expandCellRangeForMerges (line 146); that helper (selection.ts:56-98) is a `while (changed)` fixed-point loop rescanning the whole rectangle per pass, and line 85 calls findMergeTopLeft, which itself scans backward to (0,0) for every covered cell (selection.ts:33-45) — up to O(area^2) per pass. The bound is peer-chosen: MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS (numeric-attrs.ts:95) is applied only to columnWidths (numeric-attrs.ts:379-382) and spans are capped at 1000 (numeric-attrs.ts:213-219), but nothing caps table.rows.length anywhere (bandBlockNumerics iterates table.rows unbounded, numeric-attrs.ts:383-412), and maxCol re-reduces over every row on each call (selection.ts:136-138). The path is reachable from untrusted presence: docs-view.tsx:257 copies a peer's sel.tableCellRange verbatim, and editor.ts:2093-2104 calls computeSelectionRects once per peer per render (the isRangeVisible check at 2095 tests only anchor/focus block ids, not the rectangle). The nested-table fallback at selection.ts:189-191 does widen what reaches the expansion. I rejected 'already-guarded' on the grounds that buildCellRangeRects (selection.ts:725-749) walks the same rect per paint: that loop is linear in area while the expansion is superlinear, so it is not an equivalent pre-existing cost. Untrusted-input-driven unbounded render-path work is the hazard this repo's own bands address (numeric-attrs.ts:205-211), so it is in the unsafe-input-handling lane.

finding.summary: The cycle-guard sweep missed two recursive parent-map walks: `moveToNextCell` / `moveToPrevCell` recurse through `blockParentMap` with no visited set
finding.evidence: This PR adds `seen` guards to six walks over `blockParentMap` on the stated threat model that a peer can write two tables whose ids make the parent chain loop (ids come verbatim from CRDT attributes; the map is built in table-layout.ts:451 keyed on those ids, so duplicate ids across two tables produce A→B and B→A). Two walks over the same map were left unguarded: `moveToNextCell` recurses at text-editor.ts:6007 after moving the caret into the parent cell, and `moveToPrevCell` at text-editor.ts:6065 does the same. With a cyclic map, Tab / Shift+Tab at a table boundary ping-pongs between the two tables until the stack overflows (RangeError out of the key handler) — the same crash the PR closes in `Doc.findBlockInCells`. Confidence is low because the Tab path may pass `addRowAtEnd`, which takes the insert-row branch before the exit branch on the last cell; Shift+Tab (`moveToPrevCell`) has no such branch.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists exactly as described. `moveToNextCell` recurses at text-editor.ts:6007 and `moveToPrevCell` at text-editor.ts:6065, both after a `blockParentMap.get(tableBlockId)` lookup (:5992, :6052), with no visited set and no depth bound. `getCellInfo` (:3789-3794) is a bare map.get with no cycle handling. The cycle premise is the repository's own documented threat model: `findOuterCellAddress` (:3891-3907) and `findOutermostTableId` (:3916-3927) both carry `seen` sets with the comment that block ids come from peer-written CRDT attributes and a looping parent chain is representable. The map is a single document-wide namespace keyed on peer-supplied ids (table-layout.ts:451, merged upward at table-layout.ts:163-167 and layout.ts:514-517/:569), so duplicate ids across two top-level tables yield A->B and B->A. Reachable from Shift+Tab (:2731) and ArrowLeft (:3063) for moveToPrevCell, and ArrowRight (:3088) for moveToNextCell; the `addRowAtEnd` early return at :5974 only short-circuits the Tab path and does not protect ArrowRight or Shift+Tab. MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (table-layout.ts:145) bounds layout recursion only, not these map walks. No guard makes this unreachable; malicious peer data drives unbounded recursion to a RangeError out of the key handler — untrusted-input handling within the security lane, same class the surrounding guards address.
